name: Big Boi
notes: The funk-rhythm half of OutKast, and the research describes it as a rhythm-section record rather than a harmony record: what is authored heavy here is the kit and the bass, not the chord stack. Three parameters carry it. (1) **Ghost snares on 16ths** — `snare.ghost.prob` 0.62 across all eight e/a positions, the densest ghost field in this batch, over a kick at `densityPerBar` [4,7] and `syncopation` 0.58. (2) **The open hat on the "&" of 4**, which the research names as a fixed placement rather than a spread, so `openHat.pos` is `["4&"]` alone at `perBar` [1,1] and a high 0.55 probability — every other entry in this batch spreads its open hats. (3) **The bass is a melodic voice, not a sub pedal**, stated in those words: `followRootsProb` drops to 0.36 (the lowest here), `anticipationProb` rises to 0.55, and the passing-tone set carries m2 for the documented chromatic approach. Percussion is a *standing* layer rather than a colour, so congas and tambourine sit at `densityPerBar` [3,5]. The dorian funk vamp is authored as the major IV over a minor i — that is what "dorian funk vamps" means as a progression — alongside the named ii–V motion. `countermelody.densityRatio` is 0.78 because the research says countermelody is "expected rather than optional", and `melody.densityPerBar` [5,10] is its "note density high". ⚠ **Confidence is medium and the inferred parameter is the tempo.** The research rates the lane instrumentation medium-high because it is sourced through OutKast and Organized Noize, but marks the band [LOW-CONF] outright: 80–100 straight with half-time sections is the paragraph's own reading, and mode 90 inside it is mine. The half-time sections it mentions are reachable through the inherited `dark church` mode rather than authored here, so this file states only the straight feel it is sure of. ⚠ `timbreHint` is `horn_stab` for the horns the research names first; the clavinet it also names has no value in the engine's vocabulary and `rhodes` is already the parent's, so the horn is what is expressible. The breakdown-to-rhythm-section and the outro vamp are authored as `sectionRules`: the bridge drops to drums and bass, and the outro keeps the band rather than the lead. This model's fill band is `smallEveryBars` 2 / `bigEveryBars` 4 with a 16th/32nd strong-weak roll; its own `gapProb` 0.22, `descendProb` 0.41 and `rampJitter` 9 keep it off both its parent's fill and its siblings'. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.3 to 0.38.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.3 over this model's 16-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [55, 87] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 46 against a bass reaching 54, an overlap of 9. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.78, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn.
